title: Bijoe Emmanuel v. State of Kerala

content.caseIdentity: Bijoe Emmanuel v. State of Kerala, (1986) 3 SCC 615
content.facts: Three school children belonging to the Jehovah's Witnesses faith were expelled for refusing, on religious-conscience grounds, to sing the National Anthem while respectfully standing during its singing.
questionsBeforeCourt: Whether compelling the children to sing the National Anthem, despite their religious objection while they respectfully stood, violated their constitutional protections.
content.ratioDecidendi: The children could not be compelled to sing the National Anthem where their refusal was based on a sincere religious-conscience objection and they showed due respect by standing; the expulsion violated their fundamental rights.
content.holding: Expulsion of the children for not singing the National Anthem violated their rights under Articles 19(1)(a) and 25(1); respectfully standing during the Anthem was not disrespect.
content.relevance: Authority on freedom of conscience, freedom of expression and religious belief in the context of the National Anthem.

sources.evidenceNote: Official Supreme Court judgment confirms the case identity, constitutional issue and holding concerning the children's conscientious objection to singing the National Anthem while respectfully standing.
